chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"When a Muslim, a Jew, and a Christian have intercourse with a woman in one purity period, a lot is drawn among them, and the child belongs to the one whose lot is drawn."

key_terms.اَلْمُلاَعَنَة: Conjugial imprecation (used in chapter title context)
key_terms.قُرِعَ: A lot was drawn / Random selection

ai.seo_question: How is paternity determined when a Muslim, Jew, and Christian all have intercourse with a woman in one purity period?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *qur'ah* (random draw) for assigning paternity when multiple men, including Jews and Christians, have intercourse with a woman during a single *tuhr*. It highlights the Shia juristic view that faith does not preclude a man from being considered for paternity in this specific legal mechanism, ensuring clarity in lineage amidst uncertainty. The ruling underscores the procedural fairness applied in cases of *mula'ana* or general paternity disputes where exclusive evidence is lacking.
